title: Mutually Exclusive Events
rights: Original teacher-authored public-safe practice, no secure assessments.

items.prompt: One fair die is rolled. Let A be even and B be odd. Which statement is correct?
items.hint: List the numbers belonging to both event sets.
items.solution: Even={2,4,6}, odd={1,3,5}; no face belongs to both, so the intersection is empty and its probability is 0.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

options.label: A
options.text: A and B are disjoint because P(A and B)=0.

options.label: B
options.text: A and B overlap on face 2.

options.label: C
options.text: P(A and B)=1/2.

options.label: D
options.text: A and B are disjoint because their individual probabilities are equal.

items.prompt: One fair die is rolled. Let A mean even and B mean at least 4. What is P(A and B)?
items.solution: The shared faces are 4 and 6. Both occur on 2 of 6 equally likely outcomes, so P(A and B)=2/6=1/3.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

items.prompt: A standard 52-card deck has four kings. Events H=draw a heart and K=draw a king. Are H and K disjoint?
items.hint: Ask whether any king is also a heart.
items.solution: The king of hearts lies in the intersection, giving P(H and K)=1/52>0. The events are not disjoint.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because there are more hearts than kings.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because the king of hearts satisfies both.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, because just one card belongs to both.

options.label: D
options.text: No, because all four kings are hearts.

items.prompt: An event records one purchased ticket from 120 tickets. 18 tickets are both weekday tickets and discounted tickets. What is the joint probability of weekday and discounted?
items.hint: A joint probability uses the full 120-ticket denominator.
items.solution: P(weekday and discounted)=18/120=0.15. The condition does not restrict the sample space, so the denominator is all tickets.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

options.label: B
options.text: 18/(all weekday tickets)

options.label: C
options.text: 18/(all discounted tickets)

items.prompt: For a particular lunch, each diner chooses exactly one of two included sides: fruit or chips. Can 'fruit selected' and 'chips selected' be mutually exclusive?
items.hint: Define one trial as selecting a single diner and their single included side.
items.solution: Because each diner selects exactly one side, one selection cannot satisfy both descriptions. Their intersection is empty and P(both)=0.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

options.label: A
options.text: No, because both sides are served in the cafeteria.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because both can be chosen by different diners.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, because each selected diner chooses exactly one side.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, because their probabilities must both be 1/2.

items.prompt: A fair coin is tossed twice. A=first toss heads and B=second toss tails. Which ordered result is in A and B?
items.hint: Find the two-toss sequence with H first and T second.
items.solution: HT satisfies both descriptions. Thus P(A and B)=1/4 and these events are not disjoint.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

items.prompt: Suppose P(A)=0.45, P(B)=0.35, and P(A and B)=0.08. Which conclusion is supported?
items.hint: The test for disjointness is the probability of the intersection.
items.solution: Since P(A and B)=0.08>0, the events can occur together and are not mutually exclusive.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

items.prompt: For one fair die, A={1,2} and B={2,3,4}. What is P(A and B)?
items.hint: Only outcomes present in both lists belong to the intersection.
items.solution: The only shared face is 2, so P(A and B)=1/6; therefore the events are not disjoint.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026
